title: Fourier coefficients under anisotropic product noise
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set with decidable equality. Let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a distinguished index $0_B$ whose basis function is constantly one. For any nonnegative integer $n$, coordinate parameters $\rho_i\in\mathbb R$ for $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, function $f:(\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\Omega)\to\mathbb R$, and multi-index $a:\mathrm{Fin}\ n\to\iota$, the Fourier coefficient of the anisotropic product noise transform of $f$ at $a$ equals $\left(\prod_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}\ n} w_i\right)$ times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$, where $w_i=1$ if $a(i)=0_B$ and $w_i=\rho_i$ otherwise.

Finite nonempty index set $\iota$ with decidable equality
